newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia stocks close higher, dynamism seen lasting.
newsitem.headline: Croatia stocks close higher, dynamism seen lasting.

text.p: Croatian stocks closed firmer on Friday with activity picking up after a slow morning and traders said the market was in a lively phase that could last several days.
"Several stocks may shine next week, although a genuine show is not expected before autumn," Boris Galic of CAIB brokerage said.

"It could be lively," Metroholding brokerage's Marko Nikolac echoed, but added this depended on the presence of big buyers. "This is a problem of all 'thin' markets where there aren't many investors. So one big buyer dictates the trend for a stock."

Eleven of 19 active issues on Friday rose, four fell and four were flat. Volume was slightly lower at 18,694 shares, turnover rose to 11.5 million from 9.6 million kuna. Weekly turnover was 39 million kuna, down from 39.6 million.
Drugs firm Pliva was most active, edging down 15 kuna to 480 on volume of 9,470 shares.
Nikolac said most of Pliva's shares had been purchased by one big buyer in afternoon trade, at a price between 495 and 500 kuna.
"Pliva's closing price does not reflect the real situation, as only the last 20 shares were sold for 480 kuna," he said.
Zagrebacka Banka rose 10 kuna to 1,970 on volume of 2,152 units. Its preference stock added 20 kuna to 1,420 and its bearer shares rose 13 kuna to 850.
Varazdinska Banka, listed alongside Pliva and Zagrebacka in the top segement of the Zagreb bourse, inched up five kuna to 220 and traders expected a renewed interest in its shares.

Brewery Karlovacka Pivovara, in which Chile's Cervecerias Unidas has a majority stake, dominated Friday's morning trade, closing the day 35 kuna higher at 500. It was the second most active issue with 2,221 shares sold.
Traders said the brewery would remain the "market's darling" next week and could reach 600 kuna in a few months, as its price was low in relation to its earnings.
Karlovacka said earlier this month it had almost doubled net profits in 1996 and expected a further rise this year.

Electrical concern Koncar rose 80 kuna to 1,280, selling 189 shares but its growth was seen as temporary, and based on the news of the agreement with Zagrebacka and Deutsche Morgan Grenfell to float its shares abroad, signed this week.
The biggest gainer, shipper Atlantska Plovidba, added 43 kuna or 31.8 percent to 178, selling 444 shares.
The biggest decliner, Dalmatinska Banka, lost 40 kuna or 10 percent to 360 kuna with 85 shares sold.
Food processor Podravka inched down three kuna to 268, with 844 shares changing hands. Chocolate maker Kras was also on the losing side, edging down four kuna to 430, with 630 units sold.
"Podravka is moving in cycles and is bound to recover in the days ahead. As for Kras, it has an annual meeting next week, which could prompt its mild growth," Galic said.
